translationStatus: Assistant translations for review; not independently verified by fluent human reviewers. Turn order, negations, conditions and unfinished amounts are preserved.

synthetic-01: Hello, is this Ujala Plumbing? I'm calling from Helpfully on behalf of a customer.
Yes, tell me. The shop is closed now; tell me over the phone.
The kitchen tap keeps dripping after being closed. Do you do this work?
Yes. But whether the whole tap or just the washer needs replacing can only be known after seeing it.
What is the charge for coming? The customer has said up to a thousand.
There is no separate charge for coming. We do the work and give one bill.
Meaning five hundred for the visit and the rest for repair?
No, I didn't say five hundred. I'll inspect it first and quote for the whole work together.
If the customer doesn't get the work done, is there still a coming charge?
If you call us that far and don't get the work done, you must pay for the travel. Send the location first before I say how much.
Okay. Can you come tomorrow at one in the afternoon?
I'll come tomorrow. I'll finish the previous site first and then leave.
Don't write a time yet. I'll call when I leave.

Two hundred and fifty to come. Wiring or a socket replacement would be extra.

No, two hundred and fifty. Not thousand. That much just for checking.
If tightening fixes it, that's included. If replacement is needed, I'll quote labour separately. Materials are separate too.
Not nine. I have to drop someone at school first. Make it ten thirty in the morning.
Tomorrow at 10:30 AM, two hundred and fifty to check. You'll quote first if more work is needed?
Yes, write that. I won't do work without telling them.

Our normal charge is eight hundred, but that isn't for this job—
No, listen, that's the total for a small cleaning job. If yours needs a machine, it will be different.
Then what should I write just for coming?
If no work is done, coming would be two— [interrupted]

Hello, the network is going. I'm just— [call disconnected]
